And in the framework of the negotiations in Dayton, an agreement was obtained between Mr. Milosevic and Mr. Tudjman which was then translated into or resulted into the so-called Erdut Agreement around I think October/November 1995 for the gradual transfer of authority of Baranja, Eastern Slavonia and Western Srem to Croatian authority. And in order to kind of facilitate that process, the remaining UNPROFOR -- and actually it should be UNCRO because the name of UNPROFOR had changed on the 30th of March, 1995. The UNCRO mission that -- or -- but -- forces that were still in that area, SBWS, became part of a new mission under UNTAES, and these groups were still there. I mean, before I arrived there in July 1996, but I think around was it April or May 1996, UNTAES conducted an operation to verify the withdrawal of the Skorpions, the groups of Slobodan Medic, which is slightly out of the scope of my report, but the group is discussed in my report. So UNTAES conducted an operation to verify the withdrawal of Skorpions and Medic from the Djeletovci oil fields where it was common knowledge, and also I visited the area a few times between 1993 and 1995, it was common knowledge that they were present at Djeletovci oil fields. Part of the exploitation of those oil fields for benefit of certain individuals in Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, as well as in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, in the next section of your report here you deal with the attitude of the SFRY authorities with respect to the existence of these units. And here you state that the Government of the Republic of Serbia is notified at the latest in July 1991 of the existence and activities of party-affiliated private armed volunteer groups. Now, in the next -- well, at the bottom of that page you referred to Vojislav Seselj. We haven't really mentioned him so far, but here you explain that he was the president of the SRS. And -- I'm sorry. Yes, now are you aware of Seselj's volunteers' presence in Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. The best-known presence consisting of the so-called Leva Supoderica TO detachment in -- which operated in OG South, whereby the name Leva Supoderica refers to the name of a neighbourhood in Vukovar, but there is SRS, so Serbian Radical Party, documentation identifying Leva Supoderica as a "Chetnik" detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. We will get to this unit in a moment, but before I would like to take you to page 153 of your report, which in B/C/S is 186. And here you state the position of the Republic of Serbia in relation to the existence of such groups. First you quote a statement by Vice Admiral Miodrag Jokic on the 25th of July, 1991. And then you move on to December 1991. Could you perhaps provide to the Trial Chamber in a nutshell what was the general position of the Republic of Serbia at the time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, these two documents or elements of information show, actually, a transfer -- a change in the attitude, whereas initially -- and, again, Admiral Jokic was an officer in the JNA brought up and raised with the principle of brotherhood and unity and very familiar with the legislation that applied at the time. He doesn't see a benefit in having party-affiliated volunteer groups, and again from a military point of view he realises the difficulties such groups pose for command and control, in particular in light of the doctrine on -- sorry, the ideology these groups adhere to. And on the other hand we see then later on, I mean December 1991 is actually very late in the conflict, then we see basically that on the level of the Government of the Republic of Serbia Jokic has already left, there is another minister of defence, that efforts are undertaken to regularise the participation of volunteers from Serbia irrespective of the fact that these are actually people who should have joined the JNA because they were able and they didn't respond to call-ups, but efforts are undertaken to compensate and recognise, otherwise, the participation of these volunteers in the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, there is a document from the 5th of December, 1991, which might help at this stage. It is 65 ter 764 at tab 223. And this is the one that you're dealing with actually at page 153 of your report, I believe. So first we appear to have a cover page here and we see the header Republic of Serbia, "Government of the Republic of Serbia." Can we go, please, to the next page in both versions. Okay. Now, we see at the top of this page that Dragan Jovanovic, a deputy of the Assembly, posed the following question which basically asks the Assembly in what way and through which measures does the Government of the Republic of Serbia intends to preserve the welfare, security of JNA reservists and volunteers from Serbia who are deployed at the front. Then he goes into a detailed explanation. And if we go to the next page, page 3, I believe we have the answer. Yes. If we can zoom in to the paragraph below "answer." You see here that there is a reference to certain provisions of the law and the sentence at the end of this paragraph states that: "With respect to these rights, volunteers are equal to military servicemen, i.e., military conscripts." What can you say about this specific sentence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Well, basically it explains what I mentioned earlier, that is, that volunteers, even if they do not meet the legal requirements because they should have joined the JNA, they will be recognised as being members of the armed forces including for what the compensation and allowances is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. On the next page, at page 154, that's 188 in the B/C/S version, you deal here with the -- let me see, it's under item -- yes, at the bottom of that page I believe you're quoting again Borisav Jovic's book. And there's a discussion between Milosevic, Kadijevic, and Adzic on the 28th of September. And on the top of page 155 you discuss here how they refer to the possible establishment of units of rebel Serbs.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Have you seen this term elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I mean, not the term "rebel" in this context, but maybe it's a translation issue. I understand it as setting up units of local Serbs. Given, I mean, that the state -- or the self-declared state structures of the Serbs in Croatia at that stage are still quite evolving, and, I mean, they're not foreseen by the SFRY legislation or let alone Croatian legislation. So the Serbs in Krajina and SBWS as well as in Western Slavonia establish -- and this starts already earlier, established their own state structures and various ministries and they adopt various legislations. They also need to develop their own armed forces. They can partly rely on TO units -- I mean, units that used to be part of the TO of the Republic of Croatia, but the Serbs withdraw or they -- in an area of the Serb majority they may have removed or they removed the Croats or the Croats leave themselves. So de facto we have Serb units and this has to be further developed, so that's a bit a way I understood the use of the term "rebel" in this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's look at some groups you describe as at page 156, which is page 191 in the B/C/S version. The first group you deal with here is the Knindzas or a group led by Dragan Vasiljkovic, aka Captain Dragan. Now, some of the documents you quote in this section here in the following pages report that Captain Dragan was involved in training units in Croatia including units in the SAO Krajina MUP at the Golubovic camp. Now, based on the documents you have seen, can you tell us approximately when does Captain Dragan become involved in the events in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I mean, again based on the documents I have in front of me or which I reviewed for the report it's at the latest in August 1991. Now, there is lots of open source and media articles about his adventures and other activities -- not, adventures, his activities in Australia prior to that and his CV, but basically in relation to the events in the Krajina, at the latest in August 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And -- now, we see here your title says: "Captain Dragan" and then comma or in parenthesis "Knindza" or "Knindzas." Is this a unit per se?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: The name Knindza -- I'm sorry, I've seen it being used in different contexts. It has been used for people who were trained, had to receive training from Dragan in Golubovic, as well as, if I'm not mistaken, when, for example, Dragan is with some of his people in the area of Glina in -- and the document is included in -- I'm just trying to check what the exact time-period is, whether it's August or whether it's later. But then I have also seen the use of the word "Knindza," which is just a kind of a word play of the word "Knin" --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: -- and then "dza" which have some kind of importance in the context of the activities we are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And is his main role in Croatia limited to training?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It's not limited to training. I mean, he's known -- he's best known for his role in training volunteers as well as Krajina MUP, but there are also documents demonstrating his involvement in operations. And I -- I mean, we didn't find many documents, but there is one including the report on the involvement of combat activity -- activities -- combat activities, I'm sorry, in the Glina area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And I believe it is on page 157 of your report, where you indicate here that documents discuss his relationship with the Serbian DB. And this one document we're looking at is a military document, I believe, which says that we are talking about an organ or personnel engaged on behalf of the MUP of Serbia." So how do you interpret this term "an organ or person engaged on behalf"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this originates from a report from someone in the security administration at the SSNO, which is sent to I believe six addressees, which is also quite significant including General Kadijevic, so it's not I would say the daily report where you just consciously report what has happened, but it's a special report. And the use of the terminology "engaged on behalf of," basically means that he has been sent by them and also his activities after having been sent are facilitated and approved or even instructed by the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: What is the significance of the fact that it is copied to the general of the army Kadijevic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Well, he is the SSNO. It would mean that it's -- that the author considers the report of high importance and that he considers that the SSNO needs to know the contents of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I believe that we do have a document which you quote - and this we will have to skip a little bit in your report - I believe at page 258, this is in the section of your Stanisic and Simatovic report, and in B/C/S the equivalent of page 258 would be 301. Yes. For the purposes of the transcript I could say that this document is 65 ter 156, tab 48. I believe that the document actually starts on the previous page, on page 257, sorry, of the English version. Yes. If we go to the bottom of that page. Do you see here a title: "Proposal to set up a new training centre"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I see that and I also stand corrected for what I said earlier that at the latest in August he becomes active because here indeed it's May 1991, so I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Now -- actually, to your knowledge, when does the Golubovic camp start operating, do you have any information in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: No, it must be between end of May and end of August. I have a vague recollection of July, but I mean I may be mistaken, but it's in that time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay and --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And this document is being sent to the secretariat of the SUP, I believe, and -- just a second, please. I'm not sure it indicates which SUP we're talking about here --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah, that's -- the difficulty with Vasiljkovic's or Dragan's document that he doesn't indicate who -- I mean which SUP. Is it the SUP of the SAO Krajina or is it the SUP in -- even in Knin or is it somebody at the ministry of the interior in Serbia, so it's not specified. I highlight the same in my report in relation to his the use of the expression "security service," because there is no body and there is no organisation at that time with that name, there is no official name, so that makes it a bit complicated as to find out to whom he was addressing this information. However, in the context of other documents and without being too speculative, it wouldn't be unusual if it had been sent to the MUP Serbia. But I cannot give a clear answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And if we go to the next page in the English version, I think in B/C/S we just need to scroll down, I believe we could see the date there. Yeah, that's the 27th of May. Now, based on the document that you have seen, what was -- what information is available on the relationship between Captain Dragan and the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: I'm just looking -- I mean, the documents of course -- there is a number of documents drafted by him -- sorry, which he sends, for example, to -- or where he mentions people -- I mean, he mentions Frenki. Now, the only context I have seen the use of the term "Frenki" in is when it refers to Franko Simatovic who was a senior member of the Serbian state security at the time and who was also active in the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Maybe on that note we could go to page 259 of your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah, indeed it's there. You had the document from this -- from the UB, from the security administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's page 302 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah, the one we had just saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: On the top of that page you discuss that on the 14th of June Captain Dragan and Frenki had a planning meeting?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Exactly, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And in the next paragraph you also quote that Frenki on the 16th of June orders the removal of all weapons from the Knin fortress to Golubic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Exactly, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, earlier you were telling us that his chief role was to train -- training in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And you mention that there is one or two instances where he or his units were involved in combat operations?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: At least according to the documents. There may have been more occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: And it's training of members of MUP of the SAO Krajina as well as TO of the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And on page 260 you provide one example, a report from Lieutenant-General Marko Negovanovic about the involvement of Dragan and his formation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We can move to -- back to your Karadzic report at page 160 where you deal with Arkan and his men. And in B/C/S that would be page 195. So it's 160 in English; 195 in B/C/S. Now, you begin this section with -- hang on a second. No, sorry. Just a second, please. At page 161 you quote a report from the security organ of the Republic of Serbia TO. Now, before I get into the details, is this consistent, did the TO also have their own security organs?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And in this report here the TO analyses the activities of Arkan and his men. We see in the first -- well, item (i) that Arkan and his assistant, aka, kum, enjoy special attention and privileged treatment by numerous ministers and other officials of the Serbian government every day. Now, here he's talking about ministers and officials of the Serbian government. First of all, how does the TO of the security organs gather this type of information?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: You mean the security organ of the TO of the republic -- of the Republic of Serbia? I mean, they have their war procedures. We can -- I mean, we have addressed regulations in the -- in the first part of the report, so they have their ways of gathering information. They may have sources. I mean, there was a lot of talk in the media at that stage already in Serbia about the activities of people like Arkan. There was a bit of I would say glorification, even if this is outside the scope of my report, but even some security organ reports of the time kind of denounced this glorification in the media, including state-controlled media, of the activities of people like Arkan as I mentioned so that's also a potential source of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, the next document I believe you referred to here is a document dated the -- no, not this one, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yeah, perhaps we could display on the screen Exhibit P103, which is at tab 93.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It's a document of the 1st of October and I believe you referred to it at page 162 of your report. In B/C/S it's page 196 of the report. Yes. Now we will see in a moment here on the screen -- yes, 1st of October. Can you tell us a little bit about the organisations to which this document is submitted to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: So it's submitted in two copies to the security administration, which is at the SSNO, as well as in one copy to the security organ of the SSNO which is separate from the security administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: And again which is quite significant because it -- I mean, you're not going to send everything to the headquarters. Instructions should have been given to filter and to only -- I mean, to share information on the basis of need to know. That means that the headquarters is only informed if there is a need to inform them because of the significance the author gives or believes that the information that he's reporting has.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And we see here the term security organ on the top left-hand corner of the document, although the rest of the header is illegible. Now, this is an information and the title is "Zeljko Raznatovic, aka Arkan, Observations." And at the bottom of this first page you see references to negative occurrences; for example, Arkan has completely destroyed a Catholic church in the village of Erdut. And if we move to the next page in the English version, the top part -- yes, the second bullet point we see a reference to together with his group he goes to Croatian houses, interrogates them, and according to his own estimation if he doesn't like what a person says, he takes a knife and cuts, words are missing here, ears or massacres them in different ways. So this information is being sent to the SSNO on the 1st of October, 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: That's what the document states, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the bottom of this page the paragraph before the end -- now, I don't know how you will treat this type of information, there is a rumour amongst JNA members, et cetera, that Arkan goes into action, et cetera, et cetera. They think that Arkan is doing it with the full support of the SDB, State Security Service of Serbia. How would you treat this sort of information?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Well, the use of the word "think" expresses an opinion which is not necessarily factual. So you would -- in order to assess the credibility of that information, you would try to seek corroboration. You would try to look at what do other sources say in relation this specific aspect, i.e., the relations between Arkan and state security of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, on the very next page, page 163 of your report, which is 198 in the B/C/S version, at the bottom of that page -- now, again, this is an intelligence report by the security organs of the 1st Military District. The date is the 9th of January. For the record, this document is admitted Exhibit P101. And there's a reference here that the information confirms links between Arkan and the Government of the Republic of Serbia, including the Ministry of Interior, stating that Arkan is openly supported by the MUP, the TO, and the MOD of the Republic of Serbia. This is one document. Have you seen other documents of the kind confirming this information?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen several documents and I've include that in the report. I mean on page 164 there is also references. And there may also -- I have to check whether in the new documents, the ones that became available after July 2012, whether there is documents that discuss similar issues. I will check during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. In fact, let me see if we have one here. Well, let's move first to 65 ter 343. This one's actually cited in another part of your report at page 241, that's from your Stanisic and Simatovic report, 65 ter 343 at tab 89, please. Yes. I believe we can see that this is a document of the 30th of September, 1991, and it is issued by the Novi Sad KVOK. Now, can you help us with this acronym if you can, military district command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yeah, we looked into that. It's not a military district like the o for "Ooblast," here the o is used for Okrugan [phoen]. My understanding is that this is more like a geographical name or a name of a geographical level, i.e., territorial level, as opposed to a military district -- sorry, a military formation level.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. And do we see here that the document is being sent to the federal secretariat for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: It's at least received by them because when you look at the text it's a stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: So my understanding is it's received by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And this is an information. Again the title is: "Zeljko Raznatovic, aka, Arkan, the Mistreatment of Volunteers." And there's a description of Arkan's behaviour here. If we go to page 2 in the English version and the same in the B/C/S version, there's a description of two JNA officers were dispatched in the area and there's a description that they encounter Arkan and this is on the 21st of September. And do you see here that there's a footnote next to Arkan's name?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Yes, I see the little 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Can we scroll down to the bottom of that page in both versions, please. Now, do you see the comment here: "Allegedly Zeljko Raznatovic private entrepreneur from Belgrade, according to the statement of the 12th and the 17th Corps OB, he is connected with the officials of the autonomous region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem and intends to dominate and rise above the JNA and the SUP in that territory." Now, first of all, can you tell us, we know about the 12th Corps. What is the 17th Corps in this context?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the 17th Corps had its headquarters in Tuzla and this is the corps that sends units to Eastern Slavonia, for example, in May 1991 when we have the clashes, early May, the clash in Borovo Selo as well as also later in Dalj as part of the mission I discussed earlier, i.e., interposing between the armed parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like you to look at another document which is 65 ter 6050. This is at tab 572.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this is one of the new documents which are not in the report. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, do you see here that at the bottom of the page, this is a document of the command of the 12th Corps on the 12th of December, 1991. To your knowledge at the time who was heading the 12th Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: General Andrija Biorcevic was at that time the commander of the 12th Corps. He took over end of October -- no, early October/early November 1991 when General Bratic was killed in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now we see various numbers here of the numerical strength of brigades.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we go to page 2 and look at item 8, I believe that item 8 in the B/C/S version is on page 1, yes. Now, do you see here the following volunteer units belonged to the ranks of the 12th Corps? You have the Baranja volunteer OdTO. Another OdTO volunteer detachment from Novi Sad, Backa Topola, and then we see Arkan OdTO volunteer detachment 70 v/o. So what can you say here about the fact that Arkan's volunteer detachment is listed as belonging to the ranks of the 12th Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Your Honours, it shows that indeed -- and Od stands for "odred" or "detachment" that Arkan's group is considered a unit of the 12th Corps which may well be also -- sorry, which has to be seen also in the context of the attitude General Biorcevic had towards people like Arkan, and I don't know whether this has been shown already in this trial, but there is a video where basically General Biorcevic praises Arkan and his volunteers and their role in the conflict, and he describes in quite clear terms what the role of Arkan is and what kind of mission they conducted during the conflict in Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And this is signed by the Chief of Staff Colonel Srboljub Trajkovic of the 12th Corps. And if you return to the first page in the English version, you will see that it is sent to the command of the 1st Military District which is the superior command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Indeed. And I haven't looked in that -- to that before, but it's dated 12th of October. May we see it in context of the SFRY Presidency order number 73 of the 10th of October --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Of December, yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS
utterances.text: Of December, I'm sorry. It's dated 12th of December and the Presidency order of the 10th of December. It's consistent because the Presidency order states that volunteer formations, even if we know that Arkan's group had a particular status given its relations with the MUP Serbia, it's -- I mean the fact that on the 12th of December, so two days after president should order Arkan's unit which is described as a TO unit is described as part of the units of the 12th Corps is consistent with the presidential order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I tender this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1684. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I believe it's the appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It is. It is indeed, Mr. Demirdjian. Thank you. Mr. Theunens, this is the end of the -- today's hearing. You will come back tomorrow at 9.00. While I'm sure that you know the drill, I have to tell you that you're not released as a witness which means that you can't speak to anybody about your testimony and you can't speak at all to any of the parties. Thank you very much. Court usher will escort you out of court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of May, 2013, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.01 p.m.,
